outputIntent: Translate one method into an executable visual route with ordered actions, observable completion checks, and failure prevention.
positioning: Not a generic checklist slide, game UI, or card wall; it is a premium field guide whose reading order and decisions are physically obvious.
contentSchema: three to seven ordered action steps
one to three pitfalls paired with corrections

layoutFamilies.topology: a diagonal route crosses four unequal workstations; each station contains one action-specific object; checklist docks near the destination
layoutFamilies.readingPath: goal -> numbered station sequence -> checklist -> success state
layoutFamilies.cameraAndScale: wide orthographic editorial view with matched station scale and clear route turns
layoutFamilies.moduleCount: one goal marker, three to seven stations, one checklist, one success signal

layoutFamilies.topology: one central decision gate divides correct and risky paths; corrections visibly return the risky path to the main route
layoutFamilies.cameraAndScale: flat editorial board with one dominant gate and secondary warning modules
layoutFamilies.moduleCount: one decision gate, two route branches, one to three warning/correction pairs, one result

physicalVisualSystem.material: crisp flat-vector shapes printed on lightly textured planning paper, precise route lines, restrained embossed step markers
physicalVisualSystem.lighting: nearly flat studio light with subtle upper-left relief on markers; no glossy UI glow
physicalVisualSystem.color: warm neutral ground, electric blue only for progress, vermilion only for risks, charcoal for structure
physicalVisualSystem.typography: large countable step numerals, concise action labels, compact checklist text, consistent baseline grid

forbiddenElements: generic icons unrelated to the action
decorative UI headings outside the whitelist
qcAssertions: step count and order match the method exactly
route direction is readable at phone size
all modules remain above the subtitle-safe band
